analysis:
Behavior change: ServingPerformanceProfile.swift:184-194 adds automaticConcurrency, which raises the unreviewed automatic serving width from 4 to 8 (legacyMaximumConcurrency) when the backend is paged, the model is on the auto-paged allowlist, and the chip is M5 Pro, Max or Ultra. EngineV2Factory+ServingPolicy.swift:28-35 wires it in through a sysctl-derived servingChipIdentity. It applies only to serving construction with automatic selection; explicit operator values and benchmark construction are unchanged. A reviewed profile still takes precedence, and `reviewed` is empty. EngineV2Bridge+ServiceAllowance.swift:35-66 adds hasPostureGatedWidth, so any width above unqualifiedMaxConcurrentRequests, not only reviewed profiles, drops back to the unqualified width under Low Power or non-nominal thermal state. This is stricter than before for explicit operator widths above the unqualified width. Admission still caps at 8 via ServingPerformanceProfiles.concurrency, and memoryLimitedConcurrency is still applied.

Threat relevance: this is a GPU/memory availability and batching change (T-010, T-029). It adds more co-batched tenants and residual KV state on the same engine (T-028, T-041), but it adds no new trust boundary, key, attestation, or authorization surface. The chip identity comes from a local sysctl on the provider and is not an authorization input; the operator already controls local concurrency. The coordinator per-model quality cap is outside this diff and was not examined.

Unverifiable here: the ProviderConfig.swift unit is an excerpt with no patch. `try self.cache.validate()` at line 555 makes an invalid [cache] section throw. load() surfaces this as parseFailed, but loadDefault() (lines 644-657) uses try? and falls back to whole-config defaults. If validate() is new in this PR, a bad cache config could silently revert to defaults for callers of loadDefault. This is unconfirmed, and the CacheSettings.validate source and the loadDefault callers are not supplied. Next pass should check them, along with unqualifiedMaxConcurrentRequests and memoryLimitedConcurrency, which are defined outside the supplied units.
